The National Office of Electricity and Drinking Water (ONEE) is a Moroccan state-owned enterprise with legal personality and financial autonomy. It is responsible for the production, transmission and distribution of electricity, as well as the production and distribution of drinking water in Morocco.
It was created following the merger of the National Office of Electricity (ONE) and the National Office of Drinking Water (ONEP), and is a central actor in the country’s energy and water infrastructure.
History
The National Office of Drinking Water (ONEP) was established in 1972 to ensure the supply of drinking water, particularly in urban and rural areas.
In parallel, the National Office of Electricity (ONE), created in 1963, was responsible for the development of the electricity sector in Morocco.
In 2012, as part of reforms of public institutions and the rationalization of the water and energy sectors, the two offices merged to form ONEE. The new entity was structured into two main branches: electricity and water.
Missions
ONEE carries out several strategic missions, including:
* planning and development of electricity and drinking water infrastructure;
* electricity generation and management of the national power grid;
* production, treatment and distribution of drinking water;
* expansion of access to drinking water, particularly in rural areas;
* management of sanitation services in certain areas;
* securing water and energy supply.
Organization
ONEE is structured into two main branches:
Electricity branch
Responsible for the production, transmission and distribution of electricity across the national territory.
Water branch
Inherits the missions of ONEP and is responsible for:
* production and distribution of drinking water;
* planning of water resources;
* management of sanitation in certain municipalities.
Role in development
ONEE plays an important role in Morocco’s economic and social development. It is involved in:
* rural electrification;
* improving access to drinking water;
* development of energy infrastructure;
* implementation of public policies related to sustainable development.
Programmes
Among the main programmes in which ONEE has been involved:
* the Programme d’approvisionnement groupé en eau potable des populations rurales (PAGER);
* rural electrification programmes;
* regional electricity interconnection projects.
